item.title: In, on, under, next to: where things are
item.explanation_text: Use a preposition to say where something is. in = inside something: in the bag, in the room, in Tashkent. on = on top of something or touching a surface: on the table, on the wall, on the second floor. under = below something: under the bed. next to = at the side of something, very near: next to the window. between = with one thing on each side: between the bank and the café. Use at for a place where you do something: at home, at school, at work, at the bus stop.
item.contrast_text: Compare: The keys are on the desk (on top of it). The keys are in the desk (inside a drawer). The cat is under the desk (below it).
item.common_error_pattern: Using in for every place, leaving out to after next, or saying 'in home' instead of 'at home'.

examples.bad: My phone is in the table.
examples.good: My phone is on the table.

examples.bad: The bank is next the park.
examples.good: The bank is next to the park.
